findings.title: Reject ambiguous priorities between full crypto providers
findings.body: DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return priority 200, so this comparator cannot distinguish them. When both default and FIPS providers are loadable, selection depends on ServiceLoader enumeration order. A configuration that previously failed startup can now silently select DefaultCryptoProvider, whose operations explicitly use the non-FIPS BC provider. Continue rejecting multiple providers at the highest priority, or explicitly select the crypto mode, while allowing the lower-priority authz fallback.

findings.title: Enforce the SEQUENCE boundary when reading child elements
findings.body: readSequence() reads an entire child before subtracting its encoded length and accepts a negative remainder. For example, 30 04 02 01 01 02 01 02 returns two integers even though the second extends beyond the declared four-byte SEQUENCE payload. AuthzClientCryptoProvider consequently accepts this malformed DER and converts it into an R/S signature instead of throwing IOException. Read children from a bounded payload and reject any child that exceeds the remaining sequence length.

findings.title: Provide a default priority for existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: Adding order() as an abstract method breaks existing implementations of this public service interface. A provider compiled against the previous interface still loads through ServiceLoader, but comparing it with the newly registered authz provider invokes a method its class does not implement and throws AbstractMethodError, preventing crypto initialization. Source implementations also stop compiling. Make order() a default method with an appropriate legacy priority, retaining the explicit overrides for the built-in providers.

findings.title: Generate the matching EC curve for each algorithm test
findings.body: The constructor generates the default EC key, which is P-256 on the standard JDK provider, for all three tests. Selecting SHA384withECDSA or SHA512withECDSA does not change that key's curve. Thus the ES384 and ES512 tests only convert 32-byte scalars padded to larger output lengths; they never exercise full-sized P-384/P-521 scalars or the long-form DER SEQUENCE length needed for P-521. Generate secp256r1, secp384r1 and secp521r1 keys for their respective algorithms so the new encoder and decoder are tested across their actual signature formats.
